where: Section 1, sentence after the vector equation
problem: The sentence says the terms 'local acceleration ∂V/∂t, convective acceleration V·∇V, pressure force −∇p, gravity force ρg, and viscous force μ∇²V' are 'all per unit volume'. The two acceleration terms are accelerations (m/s²), not force per unit volume; only ρ times them is force per unit volume. A student can end up quoting ∂V/∂t with units of N/m³.
fix: Say: 'The left side is density times acceleration, that is, force per unit volume. The pressure, gravity and viscous terms are also force per unit volume: −∇p, ρg and μ∇²V respectively.' Keep 'per unit volume' for the force terms only.

problem: The vertical axis is labelled u/u_max, but the Couette line rises from 0 to 1 in units of the plate speed U, while the parabola peaks at 1 in units of the Poiseuille maximum. The two series use different reference speeds, so the figure suggests the Couette surface speed equals the Poiseuille peak speed, which is true only in a special case.
fix: Plot Couette as (U/u_max)(y/h) so both curves share the u_max scale, or label the axis 'u divided by a reference speed' and say in the caption which reference each curve uses.

where: Worked example step 5 and quiz Q5 answer
problem: The discharge per metre width is written as '2.5 × 10⁻⁴ m²/s per metre width'. The quantity q = mean × h already is the discharge per metre of width, with unit m²/s (equivalently m³/s per metre of width). Adding 'per metre width' to m²/s gives the wrong dimension, m/s.
fix: Write 'q = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ m²/s (that is, 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ m³/s per metre of width)', and similarly '2.133 × 10⁻⁴ m²/s' in Q5.
